correctness.rationale: With y=ell+1 the Peter–Weyl scalar has the sign of a_y+b(a_{y-1}+a_{y+1}); division by the irrep dimension does not change the sign. The neighbor-ratio tail is 2+12/y^2+O(y^-4), so the maximum is attained and exceeds 2. An independent exact symbolic check recovered both the x-derivative (the prime in Step 2 is partial_x at fixed q) and the polynomial for the adjacent difference. R_2>R_1; for q<=0 the displayed polynomial is positive on x>=2, while for q>0 it has a unique sign change in x>1 by its u-derivative and its value at u=1. Strict continuous unimodality precludes nonadjacent or triple maximizing ties. Descartes plus the endpoint signs gives a unique positive adjacent crossing; unimodality at a tie orders the next crossing strictly later. The crossings cannot accumulate at a finite q, since at any q beyond that bound all integer ratios from index 2 would then strictly increase, contrary to their tail. Scaling u=qt locates the continuous turning point at u/q tending to 3; the discrete maximum is one of its two integer neighbors. In this range the central second difference of a divided by a equals a''/a+O(q^-2)=12(x^2-q)/(x^2+q)^2+O(q^-2), giving the sharp large-mass formula. At a PSD threshold the finitely many missing blocks can only support a measure with a finite Fourier polynomial density; a nonzero finite atomic measure cannot have such a density. For uniform density, a missing matrix block annihilates the RKHS by a Haar-functional, whereas positive weights everywhere include all matrix coefficients. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed. Separate bisection on the exact-ratio expression at y=2,3 corroborated the given approximate roots.
